accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes ILO Convention 138?
o: It deals with online child sexual abuse
It concerns the minimum age for admission to employment
It establishes the Child Labour Rehabilitation-cum-Welfare Fund
It prohibits the worst forms of child labour
accepted.x: ILO Convention 138 concerns the minimum age for admission to employment. Convention 182 deals with the worst forms of child labour.
accepted.tq: Use the subject-based distinction between the two closely related ILO conventions.
accepted.sec: International and judicial standards - ILO 138 and 182, M.C. Mehta v. State of TN

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding ILO Conventions and India:
1. India ratified ILO Convention 138 in 2017.
2. India ratified ILO Convention 182 in 2017.
3. Convention 182 concerns the worst forms of child labour.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Convention 138 concerns minimum age for employment, while Convention 182 concerns the worst forms of child labour; India ratified both in 2017.
accepted.tq: Check the shared year first, then distinguish the subjects of Conventions 138 and 182.
accepted.sec: International and judicial standards - ILO 138 and 182, M.C. Mehta v. State of TN

accepted.s: The judgment in M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu (1996) is popularly associated with which case?
accepted.x: M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu (1996) is associated with the Sivakasi case involving child labour in hazardous industries.
accepted.tq: Identify the landmark case through its popularly associated location or event.
accepted.sec: International and judicial standards - ILO 138 and 182, M.C. Mehta v. State of TN

accepted.s: With reference to the directions issued in M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu, which one of the following is correct?
o: The offending employer pays ₹20,000 per child into a Child Labour Rehabilitation-cum-Welfare Fund
The offending employer pays ₹5,000 per child directly to the child as compensation
The State pays ₹20,000 per child to the employer for rehabilitation
The family pays ₹20,000 per child into a welfare fund
accepted.x: The employer was directed to deposit ₹20,000 for each child into the Child Labour Rehabilitation-cum-Welfare Fund.
accepted.tq: Match the amount with the authority responsible for making the payment.
accepted.sec: International and judicial standards - ILO 138 and 182, M.C. Mehta v. State of TN

accepted.s: Under the directions in the Sivakasi case, what alternative assistance was the State required to provide when it could not give a job to an adult member of the affected family?
accepted.x: The State was required either to provide a job to an adult member of the family or to pay ₹5,000 per child.
accepted.tq: Separate the employer’s ₹20,000 liability from the State’s alternative ₹5,000 assistance.
accepted.sec: International and judicial standards - ILO 138 and 182, M.C. Mehta v. State of TN

accepted.s: Which of the following directions was NOT associated with the Supreme Court’s Sivakasi directions?
o: Provision of education to the child
Automatic imprisonment of every employer without any welfare-fund contribution
Withdrawal of children from hazardous industries
accepted.x: The directions included withdrawal, rehabilitation, education and monetary contributions to the welfare fund. Automatic imprisonment without the specified welfare-fund arrangement was not the stated direction.
accepted.tq: Find the option that introduces a remedy not included in the stated judicial directions.
accepted.sec: International and judicial standards - ILO 138 and 182, M.C. Mehta v. State of TN

accepted.s: Which one of the following cases held that child labour in construction violates fundamental rights?
o: M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu (1996)
Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India (2011)
accepted.x: PUDR v. Union of India (1982) held that child labour in construction violates fundamental rights.
accepted.tq: Use the case-year pairing to distinguish judicial precedents.
accepted.sec: International and judicial standards - ILO 138 and 182, M.C. Mehta v. State of TN

accepted.s: Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India (2011) is associated with which of the following?
o: Minimum age for admission to employment
Stricter enforcement, rescue and rehabilitation of child labourers
accepted.x: The 2011 Bachpan Bachao Andolan case emphasised stricter enforcement and the rescue and rehabilitation of child labourers.
accepted.tq: Match the case with its distinctive judicial emphasis rather than its subject alone.
accepted.sec: International and judicial standards - ILO 138 and 182, M.C. Mehta v. State of TN

accepted.s:
Arrange the following laws in chronological order:
A. Juvenile Justice Act, 2015
B. Children Act, 1960
C. Juvenile Justice Act, 1986
D. Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000
accepted.x: The correct sequence is Children Act 1960, Juvenile Justice Act 1986, JJ Act 2000 and JJ Act 2015.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest laws first, then place the 1986 and 2000 Acts between them.
accepted.sec: Earlier juvenile laws and the trigger for 2015

accepted.s: The Children Act, 1960, primarily applied to which area?
o: All States and Union Territories uniformly
accepted.x: The Children Act, 1960 was enacted for Union Territories.
accepted.tq: Test the territorial scope of the earlier juvenile law directly.
accepted.sec: Earlier juvenile laws and the trigger for 2015

accepted.s: Which feature distinguished the Juvenile Justice Act, 1986?
o: It was the first uniform juvenile law, prescribing different ages for boys and girls
It prescribed a uniform age of 18 years for all children
It applied exclusively to Union Territories
It introduced the transfer system for 16–18-year-olds
accepted.x: The Juvenile Justice Act, 1986 was the first uniform law and prescribed an age of 16 years for boys and 18 years for girls.
accepted.tq: Compare the age provisions and territorial scope of successive juvenile laws.
accepted.sec: Earlier juvenile laws and the trigger for 2015

accepted.s: Under the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000, the age of a juvenile was made uniform at:
accepted.x: The JJ Act, 2000 prescribed a uniform age of 18 years and was amended in 2006.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the uniform age under the 2000 Act from the gender-based ages under the 1986 Act.
accepted.sec: Earlier juvenile laws and the trigger for 2015

accepted.s: The Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 came into force on:
accepted.x: The Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 came into force on 15 January 2016.
accepted.tq: Use the exact commencement date rather than the year of enactment.
accepted.sec: Earlier juvenile laws and the trigger for 2015

accepted.s: The punitive turn associated with the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 followed which event?
o: The Delhi gang rape case of 2012
The enactment of the CPCR Act in 2005
accepted.x: The 2015 Act followed the punitive policy response triggered by the Delhi gang rape case of 2012.
accepted.tq: Link the legislative change to the event that acted as its immediate trigger.
accepted.sec: Earlier juvenile laws and the trigger for 2015

accepted.s: Which provision was introduced by the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 in relation to children aged 16–18 years?
o: A uniform age of 14 years for employment
A transfer system for certain cases
accepted.x: The JJ Act, 2015 introduced a transfer system for certain children in the 16–18 age group.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific change rather than assuming that the Act abolished juvenile protection entirely.
accepted.sec: Earlier juvenile laws and the trigger for 2015

accepted.s: According to the reported NCRB 2024 information, crimes against children in 2024 increased by approximately:
accepted.x: Crimes against children were reported to have increased by about 6% in 2024.
accepted.tq: Select the approximate percentage rather than confusing it with the long-term increase since 2013.
accepted.sec: NCRB data on crimes against children - top states, child marriage by state

accepted.s: Which category constituted the largest share of crimes against children in the reported 2024 data?
accepted.x: Kidnapping and abduction were reported as the largest categories of crimes against children in 2024.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the largest crime category from other forms of child abuse and exploitation.
accepted.sec: NCRB data on crimes against children - top states, child marriage by state

accepted.s: According to the reported NCRB 2024 comparison, crimes against children had increased since 2013 by:
accepted.x: The reported increase in crimes against children since 2013 was 204.6%.
accepted.tq: Read the base year and percentage together to avoid confusing the long-term figure with the one-year rise.
accepted.sec: NCRB data on crimes against children - top states, child marriage by state

accepted.s: What percentage of child sexual-abuse offenders were reported to be known to the child according to NCRB 2021 data?
accepted.x: NCRB 2021 data reported that 97.1% of child sexual-abuse offenders were known to the child.
accepted.tq: Use the precise percentage and distinguish it from the broader finding on abusers in positions of trust.
accepted.sec: NCRB data on crimes against children - top states, child marriage by state

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about child marriage data:
1. More than 27% of women aged 20–24 were reported to have been married before attaining 18 years in one NFHS-5 figure.
2. A newer reported figure for women married before 18 years is 23.3%.
3. The 100-Day Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat campaign was launched by the Ministry of Women and Child Development in December 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct as reported. The two percentages represent different reported figures, and the MWCD launched the campaign in December 2025.
accepted.tq: Keep closely related percentages separate and verify the campaign’s ministry and launch date.
accepted.sec: NCRB data on crimes against children - top states, child marriage by state

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly matches a child-protection mechanism with its function?
o: POCSO e-Box — online complaints of child sexual abuse
accepted.x: The POCSO e-Box provides an online mechanism for complaints of child sexual abuse.
accepted.tq: Match each mechanism with its immediate operational purpose.
accepted.sec: Child helplines and reporting - CHILDLINE, 112, POCSO e-Box

accepted.s: CHILDLINE 1098 is best described as:
o: An online portal exclusively for cybercrime complaints
A statutory commission for monitoring the RTE Act
A 24×7 child helpline integrated with ERSS-112
A judicial body for transferring juveniles aged 16–18 years
accepted.x: CHILDLINE 1098 is a 24×7 child helpline and is now integrated with ERSS-112.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a helpline from a portal, commission and judicial mechanism.
accepted.sec: Child helplines and reporting - CHILDLINE, 112, POCSO e-Box

accepted.s: The POCSO e-Box was launched in 2016 by the:
o: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
State Commission for Protection of Child Rights alone
Ministry of Home Affairs’ Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre
accepted.x: The POCSO e-Box was launched in 2016 by the NCPCR for online complaints of child sexual abuse.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who launched it?’ test to distinguish the NCPCR from cybercrime authorities.
accepted.sec: Child helplines and reporting - CHILDLINE, 112, POCSO e-Box

accepted.s: The portal cybercrime.gov.in is used particularly for reporting:
o: Cases relating exclusively to child marriage registration
Child sexual abuse material and other online abuse
Physical abuse occurring only in schools
Violations of minimum employment age only
accepted.x: The cybercrime portal cybercrime.gov.in is used for CSAM and other online abuse, under the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre and the Ministry of Home Affairs.
accepted.tq: Identify the reporting channel from the nature of the abuse—online rather than physical or institutional.
accepted.sec: Child helplines and reporting - CHILDLINE, 112, POCSO e-Box

accepted.s: Which one of the following is an example of physical child abuse by omission?
o: Using the child for sexual stimulation
accepted.x: Medical or nutritional neglect is physical abuse by omission. Beating and burning are examples of physical abuse by commission.
accepted.tq: Distinguish acts of commission from acts of omission within physical abuse.
accepted.sec: Forms of child abuse

accepted.s: Using a child for sexual stimulation is classified as:
accepted.x: Using a child for sexual stimulation constitutes sexual abuse or child sexual abuse.
accepted.tq: Match the conduct directly with the legally and socially recognised form of abuse.
accepted.sec: Forms of child abuse

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT an example of emotional or non-physical child abuse?
accepted.x: Child prostitution is a form of social abuse. Verbal battering, educational neglect and fostering delinquency are emotional or non-physical forms of abuse.
accepted.tq: Find the item belonging to the neighbouring social-abuse category.
accepted.sec: Forms of child abuse

accepted.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of forms of social child abuse?
o: Infanticide, child marriage, child prostitution and beggary
Verbal battering, educational neglect and fostering delinquency
Drug abuse, stealing, school dropout and trauma
Beating, burning, medical neglect and nutritional neglect
accepted.x: Infanticide, child marriage, child prostitution and beggary are identified as forms of social abuse.
accepted.tq: Classify all items in a group and eliminate groups containing consequences or other abuse categories.
accepted.sec: Forms of child abuse

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding online child abuse:
1. More than 4.5 lakh cases were reported in India in 2023.
2. Such cases are dealt with under the Information Technology Act, 2000.
3. The IT Rules, 2021 require large platforms to detect CSAM automatically.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Online abuse and CSAM are dealt with under the IT Act, 2000, and the IT Rules, 2021 require large platforms to detect CSAM automatically.
accepted.tq: Verify the figure, governing law and platform obligation as three separate components.
accepted.sec: Forms of child abuse

accepted.s: Which statement best reflects the relationship between child labour and abuse in India?
o: Debt bondage affects only adults and cannot involve children
Child labour is unrelated to exploitation when the child works within the family
Debt bondage in child labour can run across generations, and India has the largest number of child labourers in the world
India has no significant child-labour problem outside hazardous industries
accepted.x: Child labour is recognised as a form of abuse; India is described as having the largest number of child labourers in the world, with debt bondage extending across generations.
accepted.tq: Reject absolute exclusions and connect the abuse classification with the stated exploitation pattern.
accepted.sec: Forms of child abuse

accepted.s: Which of the following is a cause of child abuse rather than a consequence?
accepted.x: Parental alcoholism is listed as a cause. Loss of self-esteem, trauma and school dropout are consequences.
accepted.tq: Separate the causes column from the consequences column before selecting the answer.
accepted.sec: Causes and consequences

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Lack of affectionate relationships — deviant behaviour
Loss of self-esteem — cause of abuse
School dropout — cause of parental alcoholism
accepted.x: Lack of affectionate relationships is a cause, while deviant behaviour such as drug abuse and stealing is a consequence. The other pairs reverse or misclassify the relationship.
accepted.tq: Use the cause-effect direction and reject reversed relationships.
accepted.sec: Causes and consequences

accepted.s: A child repeatedly exposed to family conflict and unsafe institutional conditions is at increased risk of which combination?
o: Only physical injury, without behavioural effects
Improved self-esteem, school retention and independence
accepted.x: Family conflict and unsafe institutions can contribute to trauma, delinquency and later revictimisation, along with other interpersonal and educational problems.
accepted.tq: Apply the stated cause-effect chain rather than treating abuse as producing only physical injury.
accepted.sec: Causes and consequences

accepted.s: The Study on Child Abuse: India 2007 covered approximately:
accepted.x: The 2007 study by the Ministry of Women and Child Development covered 13 states and about 12,447 children.
accepted.tq: Retain the state count and sample size as a paired numerical fact.
accepted.sec: Study on Child Abuse: India 2007 (MWCD) - key findings

accepted.s: According to the Study on Child Abuse: India 2007, what proportion of children faced physical abuse?
accepted.x: The study found that two out of three children faced physical abuse.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the proportion for physical abuse from the separate percentage for sexual abuse.
accepted.sec: Study on Child Abuse: India 2007 (MWCD) - key findings

accepted.s: What percentage of children in the Study on Child Abuse: India 2007 reported one or more forms of sexual abuse?
accepted.x: The study reported that 53.22% of children experienced one or more forms of sexual abuse.
accepted.tq: Use the exact decimal percentage instead of substituting the separate child-marriage figures.
accepted.sec: Study on Child Abuse: India 2007 (MWCD) - key findings

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the abusers identified in the Study on Child Abuse: India 2007 is correct?
o: All abusers were strangers to the child
Over 50% were known to the child or were in a position of trust
Less than 10% were known to the child or held a position of trust
The study found no relationship between trust and abuse
accepted.x: The study found that over 50% of abusers were known to the child or were in a position of trust.
accepted.tq: Use the relationship-of-trust finding to reject the stranger-only assumption.
accepted.sec: Study on Child Abuse: India 2007 (MWCD) - key findings

accepted.s: Which conclusion was drawn regarding the relative risk faced by boys and girls in the Study on Child Abuse: India 2007?
o: Only girls faced a significant risk
Only boys faced a significant risk
Boys were as much at risk as girls
Neither boys nor girls faced significant risk
accepted.x: The study concluded that boys were as much at risk as girls.
accepted.tq: Test the stated gender comparison without assuming that abuse affects only one sex.
accepted.sec: Study on Child Abuse: India 2007 (MWCD) - key findings

accepted.s: Which of the following states and Union Territory were reported to have the highest child-abuse rates in the Study on Child Abuse: India 2007?
o: Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Punjab and Rajasthan
Bihar, Goa, Odisha and Tamil Nadu
Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Bihar and Delhi
accepted.x: The highest abuse rates were reported in Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Bihar and Delhi.
accepted.tq: Recall the complete high-rate group and avoid replacing members with nearby state names.
accepted.sec: Study on Child Abuse: India 2007 (MWCD) - key findings
